content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2 (overtime for 16 general agents, break shifts, callbacks and late chat deflection) for ₹3,852, but involve the duty manager: it lifts 13:15-15:15 service level only to 59.9%, well short of the 80% target.","why":"Payments calls are taking much longer, not arriving in greater numbers. Handle time rose from about 306 s to 561 s against a 295 s forecast, in line with P2 incident INC-20261102-2029 (core banking screens freezing, account-summary API over 8 s). Service level has dropped to 2.2%, with 69 abandons in the 12:15 interval. No compliant plan reaches 80%. R2 is the best one that follows policy. It predicts 59.9% on both queues (payments 59.9%, general 59.9%) and cuts abandons to 10.0%, compared with 46.6% and 15.4% if we do nothing. Rest of day recovers to 85.3%.","trade_offs":["Against R1 (₹3,600, 57.3%): R2 adds ₹252 and 2.6 points, and payments improves from 57.0% to 59.9%.","Against P1 (free, 48.1%, 13.2% abandon): R2 costs ₹3,852 but gives nearly 12 points more and fewer abandoned customers.","P4 (64.4%) and P2 (55.8%) score higher or similar but breach CX-01. The outage message targets upi_payment_failed, which is not a rising reason, so they are excluded.","R2 balances the two queues evenly. P3 (57.0%) leaves general lower at 52.4%.","Delayed breaks and overtime add agent fatigue during an already stressful incident."],"watch":"Escalate now. Even the best compliant plan is predicted at about 60%, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). The duty manager should decide on further levers and push for incident resolution. Track payments handle time against 561 s and incident INC-20261102-2029 status, overtime uptake (16 agents needed), and payments service level once breaks shift at 14:15."}
